arXiv:2204.01980v2 [math.NT] 20 Apr 2022

Some explicit estimates for the error term in the prime number theorem

Daniel R. Johnston and Andrew Yang Address: School of Science, The University of New South Wales, Canberra, Australia Email address: daniel.johnston@adfa.edu.au Address: School of Science, The University of New South Wales, Canberra, Australia Email address: andrew.yang1@adfa.edu.au
Date: August 24, 2026
Abstract.

By combining and improving recent techniques and results, we provide explicit estimates for the error terms |π⁡(x)−li⁡(x)||\pi(x)-\li(x)|, |θ⁡(x)−x||\theta(x)-x| and |ψ⁡(x)−x||\psi(x)-x| appearing in the prime number theorem. For example, we show for all x≥2x\geq 2 that |ψ⁡(x)−x|≤9.39​x​(log⁡x)1.515​exp⁡(−0.8274​log⁡x)|\psi(x)-x|\leq 9.39x(\log x)^{1.515}\exp(-0.8274\sqrt{\log x}). Our estimates rely heavily on explicit zero-free regions and zero-density estimates for the Riemann zeta-function, and improve on existing bounds for prime-counting functions for large values of xx.

1. Introduction

1.1. Overview

Let

π(x)=∑p≤x1,θ(x)=∑p≤xlogpandψ(x)=∑pm≤xlogp\pi(x)=\sum_{p\leq x}1,\quad\theta(x)=\sum_{p\leq x}\log p\quad\text{and}\quad\psi(x)=\sum_{p^{m}\leq x}\log p

denote the standard prime-counting functions (see e.g. [Apo13, Chapter 4]). The prime number theorem is equivalent to any of the statements

π(x)∼li(x),θ(x)∼x,orψ(x)∼x,\pi(x)\sim\li(x),\quad\theta(x)\sim x,\quad\text{or}\quad\psi(x)\sim x,

where li⁡(x)=∫0x1log⁡t​𝑑t\li(x)=\int_{0}^{x}\frac{1}{\log t}\mathrm{d}t is the logarithmic integral. At the core of many results in analytic number theory are sharp estimates on the functions

|π⁡(x)−li⁡(x)|,|θ⁡(x)−x|and|ψ⁡(x)−x|.|\pi(x)-\li(x)|,\quad|\theta(x)-x|\quad\text{and}\quad|\psi(x)-x|. (1.1)

As a result, many authors [RS62, FK15, Tru16, Axl18, B“”ut18, Dus18, PT21a, Bro+21] have obtained explicit bounds on these functions. In particular, Platt and Trudgian [PT21a, Theorem 1] recently employed an argument due to Pintz [Pin80, Theorem 1] to provide estimates of the form

|ψ⁡(x)−x|≤A​(log⁡x)B​exp⁡(−C​log⁡x)|\psi(x)-x|\leq A(\log x)^{B}\exp(-C\sqrt{\log x}) (1.2)

for some positive constants AA, BB and CC, and x≥exp⁡(1000)x\geq\exp(1000). They also give related estimates for |θ⁡(x)−x||\theta(x)-x| and |π⁡(x)−li⁡(x)||\pi(x)-\li(x)| [PT21a, Corollaries 1 and 2].

In this paper we make refinements to Platt and Trudgian’s method, in turn giving improvements to their estimates that hold for a wider range of xx. Most notably, we modify a technique recently employed by Broadbent et al. [Bro+21, Section A.2] and make use of a new explicit error term for the Riemann-von Mangoldt formula [CHJ21]. We also give improvements to other preliminary results in [PT21a] by incorporating a recent verification of the Riemann hypothesis up to height 3⋅10123\cdot 10^{12} [PT21]. Some of these improvements are also discussed in [CHJ21, Section 6].

1.2. Statement of results

We obtain the following bounds for |ψ⁡(x)−x||\psi(x)-x|.

Theorem 1.1.

For all x≥2x\geq 2,

|ψ⁡(x)−x|≤9.39​x​(log⁡x)1.515​exp⁡(−0.8274​log⁡x).|\psi(x)-x|\leq 9.39x(\log x)^{1.515}\exp(-0.8274\sqrt{\log x}). (1.3)

More generally, for corresponding values of XX, AA, BB, CC and ϵ0\epsilon_{0} in Table 1,

|ψ⁡(x)−x|≤A​x​(log⁡x)B​exp⁡(−C​log⁡x)|\psi(x)-x|\leq Ax(\log x)^{B}\exp\left(-C\sqrt{\log x}\right) (1.4)

and

|ψ⁡(x)−x|≤ϵ0​x|\psi(x)-x|\leq\epsilon_{0}x

for all log⁡x≥X\log x\geq X.

Notably, our values of ϵ0\epsilon_{0} in Table 1 are an order of magnitude smaller than the corresponding values in [PT21a, Table 1] or [CHJ21, Table 1].

From Theorem 1.1, we then apply standard procedures (see Section 4) to obtain similar results for |θ⁡(x)−x||\theta(x)-x| and |π⁡(x)−li⁡(x)||\pi(x)-\li(x)| (cf. [PT21a, Corollaries 2 and 3]).

Corollary 1.2.

For corresponding values of XX, AA, BB and CC in Table 1,

|θ⁡(x)−x|≤A1​x​(log⁡x)B​exp⁡(−C​log⁡x)for all​log⁡x≥X,\displaystyle|\theta(x)-x|\leq A_{1}x(\log x)^{B}\exp(-C\sqrt{\log x})\quad\text{for all}\ \log x\geq X, (1.5)

where A1=A+0.01A_{1}=A+0.01.

Corollary 1.3.

For all x≥2x\geq 2,

|π⁡(x)−li⁡(x)|≤9.59​x​(log⁡x)0.515​exp⁡(−0.8274​log⁡x).\displaystyle|\pi(x)-\li(x)|\leq 9.59x(\log x)^{0.515}\exp(-0.8274\sqrt{\log x}). (1.6)

We also we give estimates of the form

|ψ(x)−x|≤A(logx)Bexp(−Clog3/5x(loglogx)−1/5)|\psi(x)-x|\leq A(\log x)^{B}\exp(-C\log^{3/5}x(\log\log x)^{-1/5})

(and similarly for |θ⁡(x)−x||\theta(x)-x| and |π⁡(x)−li⁡(x)||\pi(x)-\li(x)|) by using an explicit Vinogradov–Korobov zero-free region for ζ⁡(s)\zeta(s) due to Ford [For02, Theorem 5].

Theorem 1.4.

For all x≥23x\geq 23, we have

|ψ⁡(x)−x|\displaystyle|\psi(x)-x| ≤0.026x(logx)1.801exp(−0.1853log3/5x(loglogx)−1/5)\displaystyle\leq 0.026x(\log x)^{1.801}\exp\left(-0.1853\log^{3/5}x(\log\log x)^{-1/5}\right) (1.7)
|θ⁡(x)−x|\displaystyle|\theta(x)-x| ≤0.027x(logx)1.801exp(−0.1853log3/5x(loglogx)−1/5)\displaystyle\leq 0.027x(\log x)^{1.801}\exp\left(-0.1853\log^{3/5}x(\log\log x)^{-1/5}\right) (1.8)
|π⁡(x)−x|\displaystyle|\pi(x)-x| ≤0.028x(logx)0.801exp(−0.1853log3/5x(loglogx)−1/5).\displaystyle\leq 0.028x(\log x)^{0.801}\exp\left(-0.1853\log^{3/5}x(\log\log x)^{-1/5}\right). (1.9)

Certainly, the estimates (1.7)–(1.9) are asymptotically superior to (1.3)–(1.6). However, the bounds in Theorem 1.4 are worse for values of xx most likely to appear in applications. In particular, the bounds in Theorem 1.1 are better than (1.7) for all exp⁡(59)≤x≤exp⁡(2.8⋅1010)\exp(59)\leq x\leq\exp(2.8\cdot 10^{10}).

In [PT21a], Platt and Trudgian also apply their results to an inequality studied by Ramanujan. Namely, they use their estimates for |θ⁡(x)−x||\theta(x)-x| to show that

π2​(x)<e​xlog⁡x​π​(xe)\pi^{2}(x)<\frac{ex}{\log x}\pi\left(\frac{x}{e}\right) (1.10)

for all x≥exp⁡(3915)x\geq\exp(3915). By substituting (1.5) for X=3000X=3000 into the equations on page 879 of [PT21a], one immediately obtains the following improvement.

Theorem 1.5.

Ramanujan’s inequality (1.10) holds for all x≥exp⁡(3361)x\geq\exp(3361).

Note that (1.10) is conjectured to hold for all x≥38,358,837,683x\geq 38,358,837,683 (see [DP15]) and has also been shown to hold for all 38,358,837,683≤x≤exp⁡(103)38,358,837,683\leq x\leq\exp(103) [Joh21].

1.3. Outline of paper

The structure of the paper is as follows. In Section 2, we state some preliminary lemmas. In Section 3, we prove Theorem 1.1. In Section 4 we prove Corollaries 1.2 and 1.3. In Section 5 we prove Theorem 1.4. Finally, in Section 6 we detail potential improvements to our results. An appendix is also included for lengthy bounding arguments required in Sections 3.3 and 5.1.

1.4. Remarks on recent correspondence and literature

Upon announcing the first version of this article, H. Kadiri informed us that she was working on similar work with A. Fiori and J. Swidinsky. Subsequently, they announced their work [FKS22]. Compared with the results of this paper, [FKS22] contains better bounds on |ψ⁡(x)−x||\psi(x)-x| for lower values of XX (X≤10000)(X\leq 10000) and at present, does not feature any corresponding results for |π⁡(x)−li⁡(x)||\pi(x)-\li(x)|. However, as [FKS22] is currently unpublished, and our results on |ψ⁡(x)−x||\psi(x)-x| for low XX are used to establish subsequent results, we have refrained from using the work in [FKS22] here.

Importantly though, H. Kadiri and G. Hiary brought to our attention an unreliable result in [Hia16] which was previously used in this work. In particular, in [Hia16] an error in [CG04] was used to compute bounds on |ζ⁡(1/2+i​t)||\zeta(1/2+it)|. Fortunately, this error can be remedied to give the slightly worse result (cf. [Hia16, Theorem 1.1])

|ζ⁡(1/2+i​t)|≤0.77​t1/6​log⁡t,t≥3.\left|\zeta(1/2+it)\right|\leq 0.77t^{1/6}\log t,\quad t\geq 3. (1.11)

For more detail on how to obtain this modified result, see [Pat21, Section 2.2.1]. The bound (1.11) has been incorporated throughout this paper, in particular in Lemmas 2.6, 2.8 and 2.9 where [Hia16, Theorem 1.1] was previously employed.

2. Useful lemmas

In this section, we list a series of useful lemmas. Most of the following results are estimates regarding the zeros of the Riemann zeta-function which follow from existing results in the literature. Throughout, we use the notation f⁡(x)=O∗​(g⁡(x))f(x)=O^{*}(g(x)) to mean |f⁡(x)|≤g⁡(x)|f(x)|\leq g(x) for all xx under consideration. Moreover, any sum will be assumed to be over the non-trivial zeros ρ\rho of the Riemann zeta-function ζ⁡(s)\zeta(s).

We begin by quoting a recent rigorous verification of the Riemann hypothesis up to height 3⋅10123\cdot 10^{12}.

Lemma 2.1 (Riemann height [PT21]).

Let 0<β<10<\beta<1 and H=3 000 175 332 800H=3\,000\,175\,332\,800. Then, if ζ⁡(β+i​t)=0\zeta(\beta+it)=0 and |t|≤H|t|\leq H we have β=12\beta=\frac{1}{2}.

Lemma 2.1 allows us to update some useful bounds on |ψ⁡(x)−x||\psi(x)-x|, |θ⁡(x)−x||\theta(x)-x| and |π⁡(x)−li⁡(x)||\pi(x)-\li(x)| due to Büthe [B“”ut16].

The following estimates hold:

|θ⁡(x)−x|\displaystyle|\theta(x)-x| <x8​π​log2​x,\displaystyle<\frac{\sqrt{x}}{8\pi}\log^{2}x, for ​599<x≤2.169⋅1025,\displaystyle\text{for }599<x\leq 2.169\cdot 10^{25},
|π⁡(x)−li⁡(x)|\displaystyle|\pi(x)-\li(x)| <x8​π​log⁡x,\displaystyle<\frac{\sqrt{x}}{8\pi}\log x, for ​2657<x≤2.169⋅1025.\displaystyle\text{for }2657<x\leq 2.169\cdot 10^{25}.

Substitute T=HT=H (from Lemma 2.1) into [B“”ut16, Theorem 2]. ∎

Lemma 2.3.

For all x≥exp⁡(2000)x\geq\exp(2000), we have

|ψ⁡(x)−xx|≤1.570⋅10−12.\left|\frac{\psi(x)-x}{x}\right|\leq 1.570\cdot 10^{-12}.

ψ⁡(x)−xx=∑|ℑ⁡(ρ)|≤T∗xρ−1ρ+O∗​(4.3128T​log0.6​x)\frac{\psi(x)-x}{x}=\sum_{|\Im(\rho)|\leq T^{*}}\frac{x^{\rho-1}}{\rho}+O^{*}\left(\frac{4.3128}{T}\log^{0.6}x\right)

for some T∗∈[T/1.8,T]T^{*}\in[T/1.8,T]. Applying the triangle inequality and the bound T∗≤TT^{*}\leq T then gives the desired result. ∎

3. Proof of Theorem 1.1

3.1. Estimates for small values of xx (2≤x≤exp⁡(2488)2\leq x\leq\exp(2488))

For 2≤x≤592\leq x\leq 59, Theorem 1.1 can be verified by a straight-forward computation. For 59<x≤exp⁡(50)59<x\leq\exp(50), Theorem 1.1 holds by Lemma 2.2. Then, to cover the range exp⁡(50)<x≤exp⁡(2000)\exp(50)<x\leq\exp(2000) we use [Bro+21, Table 8]. Finally, for exp⁡(2000)<x≤exp⁡(2488)\exp(2000)<x\leq\exp(2488) we apply Lemma 2.3.

3.2. Proof of Theorem 1.1 for X≤10000X\leq 10000

Let X≤10000X\leq 10000 correspond to one of the initial rows of Table 1. Suppose x≥x0x\geq x_{0} where x0=exp⁡(X)x_{0}=\exp(X) except in the case X=log⁡2X=\log 2 whereby we set x0=exp⁡(2488)x_{0}=\exp(2488) and use Section 3.1 to cover smaller values of xx. In what follows, we build on the methods from [PT21a, Section 3] and [Bro+21, Section A.2]. To begin with, we set T=exp⁡(2​log⁡x/R0)T=\exp(2\sqrt{\log x/R_{0}}) where R0=5.5666305R_{0}=5.5666305 as in Lemma 2.7. By Lemma 2.4

6. Further possible improvements

There are many estimates from recent literature that go into our results, several of which are frequently updated as new techniques and computational power become available. We bring particular attention to the zero-free regions in Lemmas 2.7–2.10. For suppose one uses a classical zero-free region of the form

β≥1−1R​log⁡|t|\beta\geq 1-\frac{1}{R\log|t|}

such as in Lemma 2.7. Then applying our method (or any variation on the work of Pintz [Pin80]) one obtains an estimate

|ψ⁡(x)−x|=O⁡(x​exp⁡(−C1​log⁡x)),|\psi(x)-x|=O\left(x\exp(-C_{1}\sqrt{\log x})\right),

where C1C_{1} is any real number less than

2R.\frac{2}{\sqrt{R}}.

Similarly, using a Vinogradov–Korobov zero-free region

β≥1−1c​log2/3​|t|​(log⁡log⁡|t|)1/3\beta\geq 1-\frac{1}{c\log^{2/3}|t|(\log\log|t|)^{1/3}}

such as in Lemma 2.10, one can prove the estimate

|ψ(x)−x|=O(xexp(−C2log3/5x(loglogx)−1/5)),|\psi(x)-x|=O\left(x\exp(-C_{2}\log^{3/5}x(\log\log x)^{-1/5})\right),

where C2C_{2} is any real number less than

(53​c3)1/5​[(32)2/5+(23)3/5].\left(\frac{5}{3c^{3}}\right)^{1/5}\left[\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^{2/5}+\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^{3/5}\right].

Thus, in either case, improving on current zero-free regions will have a large impact on our results. In this direction, we note that the zero-free region due to Mossinghoff and Trudgian [MT15] has yet to be updated with the most recent Riemann height (Lemma 2.1). Moreover, Mossinghoff and Trudgian’s zero-free region is stated for all |t|≥2|t|\geq 2. It would thus be very useful if their result could be improved/generalised for the larger values of tt required in our application.

The other zero-free regions we employ are due to Ford [For02], which have not been updated (since 2002) with recent estimates involving ζ⁡(s)\zeta(s).

We also remark that the main inefficiency in our method is bounding (see (3.5))

∫tktk+1d​N​(σ,t)=N⁡(σ,tk+1)−N⁡(σ,tk).\int_{t^{k}}^{t_{k+1}}dN(\sigma,t)=N(\sigma,t_{k+1})-N(\sigma,t_{k}). (6.1)

Namely, we use the trivial bound N⁡(σ,tk+1)−N⁡(σ,tk)≤N⁡(σ,tk+1)N(\sigma,t_{k+1})-N(\sigma,t_{k})\leq N(\sigma,t_{k+1}). It would thus be interesting to further the work in [KLN18] to produce zero-density estimates in different intervals. That is, one could bound the number of zeros of ζ⁡(s)\zeta(s) in the box σ<ℜ⁡(s)<1\sigma<\Re(s)<1 and T0<ℑ⁡(s)<TT_{0}<\Im(s)<T for some choice of T0T_{0} (not necessarily 0). This would lead to an improved upper bound for (6.1).
